text:
Florida controlled most of this game and still lost it. FLA finished with 57 percent in the deserved-to-win measure, 63 shot attempts to BUF's 49, and 3.63 expected goals to 3.48, yet Buffalo skated off 5-3 winners. The gap was at even strength, where BUF out-chanced FLA 2.33 to 1.23 in expected goals. Florida's edge came from power plays, which produced 2.17 expected goals on four chances.

Buffalo built its lead early. Josh Doan scored at 5:58 of the first, Anton Lundell tied it, and Rasmus Dahlin put BUF back ahead on a power-play slap shot before the period ended. BUF out-chanced FLA 1.50 to 0.73 in expected goals over those 20 minutes. Florida took over the second period, 1.70 to 1.00, and Sam Reinhart scored twice on the power play to level it at 3-3 (the first came on an 88 percent chance, the kind of look that rarely stays out).

The decision came in the third. Noah Ostlund broke the tie on a power play at 7:15, and Tage Thompson added the fifth at 13:20 to seal it. Akira Schmid allowed 1.3 goals more than the 21 shots he faced deserved, and Jacob Markstrom was half a goal worse than expected over his 11. Buffalo got a clean 13 saves on 14 shots from Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen to start. Owen Power logged 26:30 and set up two goals, and Jack Quinn added two assists.
